q: Biology is the _____ of Life.
e: Biology is the Science of Life. Biology systematically studies plants, animals, and microorganisms. History is not Science.

q: Morphology is the study of _____ and form.
e: Morphology is the study of structure and form. Structure is the form and arrangement of parts in an organism. Chemical is different: biochemistry looks at chemical substances and chemical processes in cells.

q: Cytology is the study of _____ structure.
e: Cytology is the study of cell structure. The cell is the basic living unit of structure and function. Tissue is different: histology is the study of tissues, a step above free cells.

q: Biophysics studies flight of bird or _____ in bats.
e: Biophysics studies flight of bird or echolocation in bats. Bats use echolocation; biophysics studies that with the laws of physics. Biophysics applies physics to living processes, such as bird flight or bat echolocation. Digestion is not echolocation.

q: Biochemistry studies _____ substances in cells.
e: Biochemistry studies chemical substances in cells. Biochemistry looks at chemical substances and chemical processes in cells. Biological is not chemical.

q: Biogeography explains distribution through _____.
e: Biogeography explains distribution through space and time. Biogeography tracks distribution of species through space and time. Biogeography explains how plants and animals are distributed through space and time. Heat and light is not space and time.

q: Biometry is Biology plus _____.
e: Biometry is Biology plus Statistic. Biometry is biology plus statistics. Biometry joins biology with statistics, not with physics. Chemistry is not Statistic.

q: Anatomy and Histology are _____ science.
e: Anatomy and Histology are pure science. Anatomy studies internal structure of organisms. Applied is not pure.

q: Biotechnology and Veterinary science are _____ biology.
e: Biotechnology and Veterinary science are applied biology. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture. Veterinary science restores and maintains animal health. Pure is not applied.

q: Agriculture breeds livestock for _____.
e: Agriculture breeds livestock for food. Agriculture and husbandry both serve food production, but they are different practices. Agriculture is crop farming; it is not the same as animal husbandry. Shelter is not food.

q: Weather changes are caused by _____.
e: Weather changes are caused by global warming. Global warming is the rise in earth's temperature from extra greenhouse gases. Ozone layer is not global warming.

q: Over fishing and _____ lead to feeding problems.
e: Over fishing and deforestation lead to feeding problems. Deforestation removes forest and can wreck habitat and climate regulation. Urbanization is not deforestation.

q: Biology is a fundamental _____ science.
e: Biology is a fundamental natural science. Natural classification tries to reflect real evolutionary relationships. Biology systematically studies plants, animals, and microorganisms. Formal is not natural.

q: Medicine restores and maintains _____ in humans.
e: Medicine restores and maintains health in humans. Medicine and veterinary science restore and maintain health. Applied biology includes medicine, which restores and maintains human health. Strength is not health.

q: Animal husbandry is farming of crops and breeding of _____.
e: Animal husbandry is farming of crops and breeding of livestock. Animal husbandry raises livestock for food and other products. Animal husbandry is breeding and raising livestock, not growing crops. Wild animals is not livestock.

q: Identification assigns a _____ name.
e: Identification assigns a scientific name. Common is not scientific.

q: Taxonomy is the study of _____.
e: Taxonomy is the study of classification. Classification groups organisms so we can name them and see relatedness. Taxonomy is the science of naming and classifying organisms. Mutation is different: a mutation is a change in DNA that may change a trait.

q: Hierarchical classification has _____ taxa.
e: Hierarchical classification has eight taxa. With domain included, there are eight main taxonomic ranks. Classification groups organisms so we can name them and see relatedness. Six is not eight.

q: Top three domains are Archaea, Bacteria, _____.
e: Top three domains are Archaea, Bacteria, Eukarya. Eukarya are organisms whose cells have a true nucleus. Archaea are prokaryotes, often living in extreme habitats, and are not bacteria. Fungi is not Eukarya.

q: Domains are subdivided into _____ levels.
e: Domains are subdivided into seven levels. Older schemes listed seven ranks; adding domain makes eight. Nine is not seven.

q: The lowest taxonomic level is _____.
e: The lowest taxonomic level is Species. A species is a group of organisms that can breed to produce fertile offspring. Genus is not Species.

q: Cladistics compares _____ to find relatedness.
e: Cladistics compares DNA to find relatedness. DNA carries the genetic code in a double helix of nucleotides. Cladistics groups organisms by shared derived characters and common ancestry. RNA is different: rNA is the nucleic acid that helps turn DNA information into protein.

q: Dichotomous means divided into _____ parts.
e: Dichotomous means divided into two parts. A dichotomous key splits identification into two contrasting choices at each step, from general to specific. Four is different: four major environment components together are called the ecosphere.

q: Keys divide groups into two categories _____.
e: Keys divide groups into two categories repeatedly. Dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek. Rarely is not repeatedly.

q: Keys progress from general to more _____ characteristics.
e: Keys progress from general to more specific characteristics. Enzymes are specific: each active site fits a limited set of substrates. Complex is not specific.

q: Thallophyta has no _____ formation.
e: Thallophyta has no embryo formation. A true embryo is part of the higher-plant life cycle; thallophytes were defined without that. Thallophytes have a simple body with no true embryo in the classical scheme. Spore is different: ferns and mosses spread by spores, not by flowers.

q: Bryophyta has spores and _____ formation.
e: Bryophyta has spores and gametes formation. Gametes are sex cells: sperm and eggs, produced by meiosis. Bryophytes are non-vascular plants such as mosses. Flowers is not gametes.

q: Pteridophyta are _____-bearing with vascular system.
e: Pteridophyta are Spore -bearing with vascular system. Ferns and mosses spread by spores, not by flowers. Pteridophytes are vascular, seedless plants such as ferns. Seed is different: seed plants are gymnosperms and angiosperms.

q: Gymnospermae are non-flowering, _____-bearing.
e: Gymnospermae are non-flowering, Seed -bearing. Seed plants are gymnosperms and angiosperms. Gymnosperms have vascular tissue and seeds but do not make flowers. Cone is not Seed.

q: Angiospermae are _____ plants.
e: Angiospermae are Flowering plants. Flowering is the mark of angiosperms. Angiosperms are flowering plants that enclose seeds in fruits. Vascular-less is not Flowering.

q: Fish have fins and body covered with _____.
e: Fish have fins and body covered with scales. Scales without feathers point toward reptiles in simple keys. Fish typically use gills; aquatic turtles more often use lungs and accessory surfaces. Hair is different: hair or fur is a mammal feature in simple vertebrate keys.

q: Amphibians have body _____ covered with scales.
e: Amphibians have body not covered with scales. Scales without feathers point toward reptiles in simple keys. Partially is not not.

q: Reptiles have four limbs or _____ limbs.
e: Reptiles have four limbs or without limbs. Four major environment components together are called the ecosphere. Two is different: dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Birds are warm-blooded with _____.
e: Birds are warm-blooded with Feathers. Feathers mark birds in a vertebrate key, not mammals. Scales is different: scales without feathers point toward reptiles in simple keys.

q: Mammals are warm-blooded with _____.
e: Mammals are warm-blooded with Hair. Hair or fur is a mammal feature in simple vertebrate keys. Feathers is different: feathers mark birds in a vertebrate key, not mammals.

q: Biologists use morphology and _____ as keys.
e: Biologists use morphology and anatomy as keys. Anatomy studies internal structure of organisms. Morphology is the study of structure and form of organisms. Ecology is different: ecology studies how organisms interact with one another and with the abiotic world.

q: Keys provide a simple way to _____ organisms.
e: Keys provide a simple way to classify organisms. Preserve is not classify.

q: Cold-blooded vertebrates include Fish, Amphibian and _____.
e: Cold-blooded vertebrates include Fish, Amphibian and Reptile. Reptiles are scaly, air-breathing vertebrates that usually use lungs. Amphibians can use skin, mouth lining, and lungs for gas exchange. Mammal is different: mammals are warm-blooded vertebrates with hair and milk.

q: Light microscope uses _____ as radiation source.
e: Light microscope uses light as radiation source. Light supplies the energy that chlorophyll captures for photosynthesis. A light microscope uses light as the radiation that forms the image. Electron is different: electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam.

q: Electron microscope uses _____ as radiation source.
e: Electron microscope uses electron as radiation source. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam. Electron microscopes use electrons as the radiation source. Neutron is not electron.

q: TEM allows us to see _____ sections.
e: TEM allows us to see thin sections. TEM sends electrons through a thin specimen to show internal detail. Thick is not thin.

q: SEM passes beam over the _____ of specimen.
e: SEM passes beam over the surface of specimen. SEM scans the surface with electrons to give a three-dimensional view. Center is not surface.

q: Condenser focuses _____ onto the specimen.
e: Condenser focuses electron onto the specimen. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam. The condenser focuses light onto the specimen; an iris diaphragm controls how much light. Light is different: light supplies the energy that chlorophyll captures for photosynthesis.

q: Objective lens is responsible for magnification and _____.
e: Objective lens is responsible for magnification and resolution. Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate. Magnification is how many times larger the image is than the real object. Focusing is not resolution.

q: Eyepiece lens magnifies but does not _____ the image.
e: Eyepiece lens magnifies but does not resolve the image. To resolve is to see two close points as separate. The eyepiece magnifies the image the objective has already formed; it does not set resolution. Illuminate is not resolve.

q: Iris diaphragm controls amount of _____.
e: Iris diaphragm controls amount of light. Light supplies the energy that chlorophyll captures for photosynthesis. The diaphragm contracts and flattens to increase thorax volume during inhalation. Water is different: water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis.

q: Electron microscope components must be in a _____.
e: Electron microscope components must be in a gas. Electron microscopes use electrons as the radiation source. An electron microscope uses electrons, not light, and can magnify up to about 500,000 times. Liquid is not gas.

q: Condenser electromagnetic lens focuses the _____ beam.
e: Condenser electromagnetic lens focuses the electron beam. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam. The condenser focuses light onto the specimen; an iris diaphragm controls how much light. Light is different: light supplies the energy that chlorophyll captures for photosynthesis.

q: Projector lenses focus image onto the _____.
e: Projector lenses focus image onto the screen. In TEM, projector lenses throw the final image onto a screen. Slide is not screen.

q: Light microscope magnifies up to _____.
e: Light microscope magnifies up to 100X. A light microscope uses light as the radiation that forms the image. 2000X is not 100X.

q: Electron microscope magnifies up to _____.
e: Electron microscope magnifies up to 500,000X. About 500,000 times is electron-microscope magnification, not light. Electron microscopes use electrons as the radiation source. 10,000X is not 500,000X.

q: Light microscope can examine _____ specimen.
e: Light microscope can examine Either dead or alive specimen. A light microscope uses light as the radiation that forms the image. A light microscope uses light and typically magnifies up to about 1500 to 2000 times, not 500,000.

q: Electron microscope examines only _____ specimen.
e: Electron microscope examines only dehydrated and dead specimen. Electron microscopes use electrons as the radiation source. An electron microscope uses electrons, not light, and can magnify up to about 500,000 times.

q: Specimen prep for electron microscope is _____.
e: Specimen prep for electron microscope is lengthy and complicated. EM specimen preparation is lengthy and complicated compared with a simple light-microscope slide. Electron microscopes use electrons as the radiation source. Fast is not lengthy and complicated.

q: Magnification is number of times larger an image is compared to _____ size.
e: Magnification is number of times larger an image is compared to observed size. Observed size over actual size gives magnification. Magnification is how many times larger the image is than the real object. Fake is not observed.

q: In $M = I / A$, $I$ is the _____ size.
e: In M = I / A, I is the Observed size. Magnified is not Observed.

q: In $M = I / A$, $A$ is the _____ size.
e: In M = I / A, A is the Image size. Actual is not Image.

q: Resolution is ability to distinguish between _____ objects close together.
e: Resolution is ability to distinguish between three objects close together. Dichotomous does not mean divided into three parts. Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate. Two is different: dichotomous means divided into two parts, from Greek.

q: Increase in magnification might make image _____.
e: Increase in magnification might make image blur. Magnification is how many times larger the image is than the real object. Darker is not blur.

q: Greater resolution means greater _____.
e: Greater resolution means greater detail. Extra magnification without resolution does not add true detail, only a bigger blur. Resolution is the ability to distinguish two close points as separate. Size is not detail.

q: Electron microscope image is recorded in _____.
e: Electron microscope image is recorded in black and white. Electron microscopes use electrons as the radiation source. An electron microscope uses electrons, not light, and can magnify up to about 500,000 times. Color is not black and white.

q: Usually _____ illumination is the light source.
e: Usually substage illumination is the light source. Overhead is not substage.

q: Electron gun emits _____ velocity electron beam.
e: Electron gun emits low velocity electron beam. Electron microscopes use an electron beam, not a light beam. High is not low.

q: Objective electromagnetic lens _____ the first image.
e: Objective electromagnetic lens magnified the first image. The objective lens both magnifies and provides resolving power. Resolves is not magnified.

q: Light passing through specimen is collected by _____ lens.
e: Light passing through specimen is collected by objective lens. The objective lens both magnifies and provides resolving power. Eyepiece is different: the eyepiece magnifies the image the objective has already formed; it does not set resolution.

q: Biotechnology combines biological sciences with _____ technologies.
e: Biotechnology combines biological sciences with engineering technologies. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture. Medical is not engineering.

q: Traditional biotechnology includes making wine, cheese, yoghurt, bread and _____.
e: Traditional biotechnology includes making wine, cheese, yoghurt, bread and beer. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture. In bread making, yeast produces carbon dioxide, which makes dough rise, plus ethanol. Metal is not beer.

q: Mesopotamia used bacteria to convert wine into _____.
e: Mesopotamia used bacteria to convert wine into vinegar. Wine yeast uses oxygen first, then ferments anaerobically when oxygen is gone. Juice is not vinegar.

q: Modern biotechnology produces antibiotic _____.
e: Modern biotechnology produces antibiotic penicillin. Penicillin is an antibiotic originally from a fungus. Biotechnology uses living systems in industry, medicine, and agriculture. Paracetamol is not penicillin.

q: Human _____ producing genes are put into bacteria.
e: Human insulin producing genes are put into bacteria. Insulin lowers blood glucose by helping cells take up sugar. Glucose is different: glucose is the hexose sugar made in photosynthesis and burned in respiration.

q: Transgenic goats produce antibodies in their _____.
e: Transgenic goats produce antibodies in their blood. Blood carries gases, nutrients, hormones, and wastes around the body. Urine is different: urine is the waste fluid formed by nephrons.

q: Transgenic plants are engineered to produce _____.
e: Transgenic plants are engineered to produce vaccine. Vaccines are an applied-biology tool for preventing infectious disease. Poison is not vaccine.

q: Microorganisms include protists, archea, fungi, bacteria and _____.
e: Microorganisms include protists, archea, fungi, bacteria and viruses. Viruses are acellular and only reproduce inside a host cell. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi. Plants is not viruses.

q: Archea and bacteria are _____.
e: Archea and bacteria are prokaryotes. Prokaryotes such as bacteria and archaea lack a true nucleus. Eukaryotes is different: eukaryotes have a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

q: Viruses reproduce inside living cell using _____ materials of host.
e: Viruses reproduce inside living cell using genetic materials of host. Viruses are acellular and only reproduce inside a host cell. Structural is not genetic.

q: Yeasts have single _____ cells.
e: Yeasts have single spherical cells. Filamentous is not spherical.

q: Microorganisms are cultured easily by using _____.
e: Microorganisms are cultured easily by using fermenters. Microorganisms are microscopic living things such as bacteria, protozoa, and many fungi. Microscopes is not fermenters.

q: Biofuel fermentation produces _____ which is distilled.
e: Biofuel fermentation produces ethanol which is distilled. Yeast fermentation turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Fermentation is microbial chemical change of organic material, with or without oxygen in modern use. Methanol is not ethanol.

q: Ethanol is mixed with petrol to get _____.
e: Ethanol is mixed with petrol to get gasohol. Yeast fermentation turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Kerosene is not gasohol.

q: In bread making, water activates _____ enzymes.
e: In bread making, water activates amylase enzymes. Amylase is the enzyme that hydrolyses starch. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Protease is different: proteases digest proteins to amino acids.

q: Yeasts ferment sugar to carbon dioxide and _____.
e: Yeasts ferment sugar to carbon dioxide and oxygen. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Ethanol is different: yeast fermentation turns sugar into ethanol and carbon dioxide.

q: Protein _____ holds carbon dioxide gas bubbles in dough.
e: Protein gluten holds carbon dioxide gas bubbles in dough. Carbon dioxide is used in photosynthesis and produced by respiration and combustion. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Keratin is not gluten.

q: Dough is baked in oven at _____ to kill yeasts.
e: Dough is baked in oven at 200^ degrees extC to kill yeasts. 200^ degrees extC is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Milk is pasteurized at about _____ to kill bacteria.
e: Milk is pasteurized at about 90^ degrees extC to kill bacteria. 90^ degrees extC is the biological term this statement needs.

q: Starter culture turns lactose to _____.
e: Starter culture turns lactose to lactic acid. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short. Acetic acid is not lactic acid.

q: Lactic acid coagulates milk protein _____.
e: Lactic acid coagulates milk protein casein. Casein is the main milk protein that clots in cheese making. Lactic acid is the product of anaerobic respiration in muscle when oxygen is short. Gluten is not casein.

q: In cheese making, _____ causes further coagulation.
e: In cheese making, rennet causes further coagulation. Rennet enzymes clot casein during cheese making. Trypsin is not rennet.

q: Grape juice is treated with sulphur dioxide to kill _____ yeast.
e: Grape juice is treated with sulphur dioxide to kill natural yeast. Natural classification tries to reflect real evolutionary relationships. Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in bread, wine, and ethanol fuel. Artificial is not natural.

q: Yeast respire aerobically until _____ is used up.
e: Yeast respire aerobically until oxygen is used up. Oxygen is released by photosynthesis and used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration. Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in bread, wine, and ethanol fuel. Nitrogen is different: nitrogen is in amino acids and nucleic acids, but it is not in every biological molecule.

q: Yeast cells die when alcohol content reaches _____.
e: Yeast cells die when alcohol content reaches 15%. Yeast is a unicellular fungus used in bread, wine, and ethanol fuel. 50% is not 15%.

q: Beer is made from barley grains which activate _____-digesting enzymes.
e: Beer is made from barley grains which activate protein -digesting enzymes. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Starch is different: starch is the plant storage polysaccharide made of amylose and amylopectin.

q: The sugary solution obtained from malted barley is called _____.
e: The sugary solution obtained from malted barley is called wort. Whey is not wort.

q: Wort is boiled with hops which give beer a _____ flavour.
e: Wort is boiled with hops which give beer a bitter flavour. Sour is not bitter.

q: Louis Pasteur described alcoholic fermentation as 'life without _____'.
e: Louis Pasteur described alcoholic fermentation as 'life without air '. Air of the atmosphere supplies oxygen and carbon dioxide for life. Fermentation is microbial chemical change of organic material, with or without oxygen in modern use. Food is different: agriculture and husbandry both serve food production, but they are different practices.

q: Fermenter tanks are made of stainless steel to withstand _____ effect.
e: Fermenter tanks are made of stainless steel to withstand corroding effect. Cooling is not corroding.

q: Hot _____ is passed into fermenter to sterilize it.
e: Hot steam is passed into fermenter to sterilize it. Water is different: water is the essential solvent of cells and a raw material of photosynthesis.

q: Enzymes are protein molecules and biological _____.
e: Enzymes are protein molecules and biological catalysts. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Inhibitors is not catalysts.

q: Enzymes do not require expensive fuel to maintain high _____.
e: Enzymes do not require expensive fuel to maintain high temperature. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Volume is different: as an animal grows, volume rises faster than surface, so simple skin exchange is not enough.

q: Microbial trypsin is used to treat blood _____.
e: Microbial trypsin is used to treat blood clotting. Blood clotting seals wounds and needs clotting proteins from the liver. Pressure is not clotting.

q: Pancreatic trypsin is used for treatment of _____.
e: Pancreatic trypsin is used for treatment of inflammation. Inflammation is a defensive response with heat, redness, swelling, and pain. Infection is not inflammation.

q: Proteases are _____-digesting enzymes.
e: Proteases are protein -digesting enzymes. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up.

q: Lipases are _____-digesting enzymes.
e: Lipases are fat -digesting enzymes. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Protein is different: proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs.

q: Proteases act on red _____ in blood stains.
e: Proteases act on red haemoglobin in blood stains. Haemoglobin in red blood cells binds oxygen for transport. Platelet is not haemoglobin.

q: Fungi produce _____ enzymes for extracting fruit juices.
e: Fungi produce pectinases enzymes for extracting fruit juices. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Proteases is not pectinases.

q: Pectinases break down pectin between cell walls and separate fruit _____.
e: Pectinases break down pectin between cell walls and separate fruit cells. The cell is the basic living unit; tissues are groups of similar cells. Juice is cleared when pectin is broken, not because cellulose and starch flood out. Seeds is not cells.

q: Break down of polysaccharides causes juice to become _____.
e: Break down of polysaccharides causes juice to become cloudy. An extra chromosome 21 produces Down's syndrome. Dark is not cloudy.

q: Pectinases break polysaccharides to sugar making juice sweeter and _____.
e: Pectinases break polysaccharides to sugar making juice sweeter and clearer. Bitter is not clearer.

q: Biological washing powders remove stains caused by blood, egg, gravy and _____.
e: Biological washing powders remove stains caused by blood, egg, gravy and grease. Biological powders use proteases for protein stains and lipases for fat stains; those jobs are not swapped.

q: Enzymes isolated from cell still retain their ability to _____.
e: Enzymes isolated from cell still retain their ability to function. Function is what a structure does in the living body. Enzymes can still work after they are isolated from the cell; that is why we use them in industry.

q: Many industrial enzymes are obtained from fungi or _____.
e: Many industrial enzymes are obtained from fungi or bacteria. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Viruses is different: viruses are acellular and only reproduce inside a host cell.

q: Both protein and fat molecules are large but enzymes digest them into small, _____ substances.
e: Both protein and fat molecules are large but enzymes digest them into small, soluble substances. Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed reactions without being used up. Proteins are polymers of amino acids with many structural and catalytic jobs. Solid is not soluble.
